Wales: Camping and Riding Combined

Wales is brilliant for motorcycle camping. The combination of mountain passes, coastal roads, and compact geography means you can ride all day and pitch up in a spectacular location every night. Welsh campsites range from wild mountain pitches to well-equipped coastal sites, all at reasonable prices.

Snowdonia

Llyn Gwynant Campsite — Lakeside pitching with Snowdon views. One of the most beautifully situated campsites in Britain. Basic facilities but the location is spectacular. Popular with walkers, climbers, and bikers. Book well ahead for summer.

Cae Du, Tywyn — Coastal Snowdonia site at the foot of Cader Idris. Mountain and sea views from the pitches. Excellent facilities and a short ride to the mountain passes.

Pembrokeshire

Caerfai Bay Campsite, St David's — Clifftop site overlooking Caerfai Bay, walking distance to St David's. Sea views from every pitch. One of the best coastal camping experiences in Britain.

Trefalen Farm, Bosherston — Near the famous lily ponds and Barafundle Bay. Small, quiet, and perfectly positioned for Pembrokeshire coast exploration.

Brecon Beacons

Priory Mill Farm, Brecon — Riverside site just outside Brecon town. Easy access to the Black Mountain Road and the Beacons passes. Good facilities and walking distance to Brecon's pubs and restaurants.

Welsh campsites are generally cheaper than English or Scottish equivalents, and the locations are just as spectacular. Budget-conscious motorcycle tourers take note.

More Recommended Welsh Sites

  • Shell Island, Llanbedr — Vast site on a tidal island with stunning beach. Access road includes a ford!
  • Hillend Campsite, Gower — Sand dune camping above Rhossili Beach, surfing and coastal walks
  • Ty Coch, Porthdinllaen — Near the famous beach pub, Llyn Peninsula setting
  • Nantcol Waterfalls, Llanbedr — Wild camping feel in a wooded Snowdonia valley
  • Beddgelert Campsite — In the village at the foot of Snowdon, river running through the site

Wild Camping in Wales

Unlike Scotland, wild camping in Wales is technically illegal without landowner permission. However, many upland areas tolerate discreet camping above the enclosed land boundary if you follow leave-no-trace principles. The Brecon Beacons and Snowdonia uplands are commonly used for wild camping. Pitch late, leave early, and take everything with you.

Practical Tips

Welsh campsite prices typically range from £8-20 per night for a motorcycle pitch. Many accept online booking; smaller sites may be cash-only. The weather in western Wales is wet — a tent with a good porch or vestibule for storing wet gear is invaluable. Carry a groundsheet and kickstand pad. Most Welsh sites have basic to good showers and toilets. Eco-friendly sites are increasingly common. Read our Best Motorcycle Roads in Wales: Passes, Coast and Valleys guide for more. Read our Pembrokeshire Coast Motorcycle Route: Wales' Coastal Gem guide for more.

faq.q: Is wild camping legal in Wales?
faq.a: Unlike Scotland, wild camping in Wales is technically illegal without the landowner's permission. However, many upland areas tolerate discreet camping above the enclosed land boundary if you follow leave-no-trace principles. The Brecon Beacons and Snowdonia uplands are commonly used. Pitch late, leave early and take everything away with you.

faq.q: How much do Welsh campsites cost?
faq.a: Welsh campsite prices typically range from 8 to 20 pounds per night for a motorcycle pitch, generally cheaper than English or Scottish equivalents while offering equally spectacular locations. Many sites accept online booking, though smaller ones may be cash-only, so carry some cash when touring rural Wales.

faq.q: Which is the most scenic campsite in Snowdonia?
faq.a: Llyn Gwynant Campsite offers lakeside pitching with Snowdon views and is one of the most beautifully situated campsites in Britain. Facilities are basic but the setting is spectacular, and it is popular with walkers, climbers and bikers alike. Book well ahead for summer, as it fills quickly.

faq.q: Where are the best coastal campsites for Pembrokeshire?
faq.a: Caerfai Bay Campsite near St David's is a clifftop site overlooking Caerfai Bay, with sea views from every pitch and St David's within walking distance. Trefalen Farm at Bosherston sits near the famous lily ponds and Barafundle Bay, making it well placed for exploring the Pembrokeshire coast.

faq.q: What gear should I pack for camping in wet Welsh weather?
faq.a: Western Wales is notably wet, so a tent with a good porch or vestibule for storing soaked gear is invaluable. Carry a groundsheet and a kickstand pad to stop your bike sinking into soft ground. Pack everything in dry bags inside your panniers, as prolonged rain will find any weak point in your luggage.
